title: 27 · pushpadanta · The Singer Who Stole Flowers
lines: n
The most beautiful hymn to Shiva was written by a thief.
n
He wrote it the night he got caught.
n
Pushpadanta was a musician of the heavens.
He could fly. He could walk unseen.
n
And every night he stole flowers from a king's garden.
To offer to Shiva.
n
The king could not catch a thief he could not see.
n
So he scattered bilva leaves across every path.
Leaves that had been offered to Shiva.
n
The thief stepped on them.
And in one breath, his powers were gone.
n
He had stolen for Shiva,
and insulted Shiva with his own foot.
n
He did not run. He did not make excuses.
He sat down in that garden, and sang.
n
If the ocean were ink, and the sky were paper,
"If the ocean were ink, and the sky were paper,
even then your greatness could not be written.
even then your greatness could not be written."
n
Shiva gave him back everything.
And the song is still sung today.
n
When you fall, do not hide. Sing. That is sadhana.
n
